The scorecards leave a few things unclear. Each one is explained below, with a one-click fix where there's a safe answer. Nothing changes until you click, and every change can be undone under Your changes.

**Catches that count for the team.** The scorecard prints only the fielder's surname, like *c Mendis*. When a side has two players with that surname (Sri Lanka's Kusal and Kamindu Mendis are both *K Mendis*), it can't say which one took it, so the catch counts for the team (in its catches) but for neither player. **Nothing to do.** If you want a player to have one, you can still pick them below.

Already sorted out for you: a catcher can't be the bowler (that's printed c & b ), a stumping is always the wicketkeeper, and a catch by a substitute fielder ( c Sub ) counts for the team but for no player, as in real cricket.
Every catch and stumping has its player.
**{len(sug)} of these have a clear answer**, usually the side's wicketkeeper or the player who takes most of that side's catches. The reason is shown under each one below.
**Or choose yourself.** {'The suggestion is already picked where there is one. ' if len(sug) else ''}Leave any you're not sure about.
Showing the first {len(show)} of {len(unc)}. Save these and the next ones appear.

**Two different players with the same name.** The game prints only an initial and surname, so two players can end up with the same name, like *R Patel* at Leicestershire and *R Patel* at Surrey. The site then adds their runs and wickets together as if they were one person. A player can't play for two teams in the same season of a competition, so each name below is almost certainly two people.
No name is used by two players.
**Keep all {len(shared)} apart.** Each name stays with the team it played most games for, and the player at the other team gets the team added to their name, e.g. *{big.player} ({big.separate[0]})*.
For a name the site didn't spot: pick the player, the team where it's really someone else, and the name to show for them.

**One player under two names.** Sometimes the same player shows up under two slightly different names. The names below look like one player: same initial and surname, same team, and never in the same match together.
No player appears under two names.

**Games from an earlier playthrough.** When you reload a save and play part of a season again, the game saves each replayed match over its old file. But a knockout with different teams gets a new file, so the old game stays in your Scorecards folder. That's how one IPL season can end up with three finals. The site spots these from when each file was saved and leaves them out of every stat. Nothing to do, unless one of them should count.
